title: Waterloo introduction
summary: What Waterloo is, what a Waterloo docstring is, and where to start.

items: Waterloo is a structured docstring format for Python code.
A Waterloo docstring is indentation-based and divided into sections and nested subsections.
Normative content is tracked explicitly via a subsection Preamble.normative_sections.
The format is designed to be both human-readable and machine-checkable.
A section is a top-level docstring block such as Preamble, Contract, or See_also.
A nested subsection is a block inside a section, for example a profile entry, a contract entry, or a list item.
The documentation and the waterlint tools may refer to nested subsections with dotted names for convenience.
Use about('waterlint.command') to learn the validation workflow.
Use about('waterloo.structure') to learn the docstring shape and indentation rules.
Use about('waterloo.markup') to learn the inline markup tokens and roles.
